main_text.l: nus Iesus det nobis omnibus castam, puram
& sanctam mentem, ut olim videre possimus

l.i: rai ad Abram: En prohibuit me domi-
nus ne parerem, ingredere quaeso ad ancil-
lam meam, si forte aedificer ex ea: & obe-
Sarai uxor Abram, Hagar Aegyptiam an-
cillam suam, a fine decem annorum, quo
habitauit Abram in terra Chanaan, et
dedit eam Abra marito suo in uxorem.
Qui cum ingressus esset ad Hagar, conce-
pit illa: vidensque se gravidam, vilipensa
est domina eius in oculis suis. Et dixit Sa-
rai ad Abram: Iniuria mea super te est:
ego dedi ancillam meam in sinum tuum,

page.notes: The initial "T" is a woodcut ornamental letter, read as T. The mark over "Abram" in "Abram" lines (printed as a small curved sign before the name) is an unidentified printed sign; it has been read as the name "Abram" without it, and the sign is not transcribed. "TAQ̄VE": the Q carries a stroke marking an omitted m, read as a macron over Q. The paragraph of the body text continues past the bottom of the page. The running head is read as NUPTIALES with the printed capitals spaced out.
